{{Quote|Gungans no dyin' witout a fight. Wesa warriors.|[[Jar Jar Binks/Legends|Jar Jar Binks]]|<ref name="Episode I" />}}
The '''Gungans''' were a sentient, [[Amphibian/Legends|amphibious]] [[Humanoid/Legends|humanoid]] race native to the terrestrial [[Planet/Legends|planet]] known as [[Naboo/Legends|Naboo]]. Prior to the [[Invasion of Naboo/Legends|Invasion of Naboo]], an event that took place in [[32 BBY/Legends|32 BBY]], the Gungans were a largely isolationist society. They were able to combine machinery with biology. They lived in large bubble-like domes under water. Gungans had strong leg muscles for swimming and were aided by their long fin-like ears. Their somewhat lanky arms ended in four-fingered hands, and their feet had three stubby toes each. Females tended to be slightly smaller with sleeker faces. They often tied their long ears back.

While most spacefarers would dismiss Gungans as primitives, they developed an advanced, albeit unique, technology. They grew the basic structures of buildings, vehicles and technology and adorned them with artistic flourishes and organic lines. This gave Gungan technology a very fluid, non-rectilinear look.

The power source for Gungan technology was a mysterious blue-white energy "goo" that was mined in the depths of Naboo's oceans. The viscous plasmic material formed the basis of Gungan weaponry as well.

The Gungans had mastered energy field technology for a number of uses. Their underwater cities employed hydrostatic fields to create large bubbles of atmosphere within which they dwell. Similarly, Gungan ground troops carried portable frames which generate a protective energy field capable of deflecting blaster fire. In large-scale combat, giant Gungan shield generators could create an immense umbrella of protective shield energy that could stop laser bolts and physical objects with great kinetic energy.

Despite mastering this bizarre technology, Gungans still employed beasts of burden for transportation. Their most common mount was the [[Kaadu/Legends|kaadu]], a wingless [[Reptavian/Legends|reptavian]] which Gungans adorned with feathers and rode into combat. Other favored Gungan mounts included the large, stubborn [[Falumpaset/Legends|falumpaset]]. For truly heavy loads, the Gungans domesticated the [[Fambaa/Legends|fambaa]], a nine-meter tall, quadrupedal amphibian.

The Gungans maintained a large standing-armed force called the Gungan Grand Army. This huge collection of foot soldiers carried [[Cesta/Legends|cestas]], electropoles, and [[Atlatl/Legends|atlatls]] capable of hurling plasmic energy spheres (or boomers, as Gungans called them). Gungan catapults hurled even larger boomers over great distances.

The Gungans were ruled by a Boss and his Rep Council from the High Tower Board Room of Otoh Gunga. The Gungans had an uneasy relationship with the Naboo, the [[Human/Legends|human]] colonists on the planet. Many Naboo looked down upon the Gungans, thinking them as primitive. The Gungans in turn tried to avoid any contact with the surface-dwellers.

Individuals were called a Gung (eg. [[Gungan Grand Army/Legends|Militiagung]]).

==Biology and appearance==
{{Quote|There was also a creature who looked like a cross between many species. He stood upright on two legs like a Human. He had a mouth shaped like a bill, and a frog's big eyes rising out of his head. He was not really that unusual compared to some of the creatures who pass through Mos Espa. But I'd never met anyone like him before.|Anakin Skywalker's description of Jar Jar Binks, the first Gungan he ever saw|<ref name="Journal: Anakin Skywalker">''[[Star Wars Journal: Anakin Skywalker]]''</ref>}}
[[File:GunganFamily-GCG.jpg|thumb|left|200px|An Otolla Gungan child]]
The Gungans were separated into two races: the lanky orange, yellow or red-skinned '''[[Otolla/Legends|Otolla]]''' race, and the heavier green-skinned '''[[Ankura/Legends|Ankura]]''' race. However, they all exhibited many of the same basic physical traits.

Starting life as [[Tadpole/Legends|tadpoles]], Gungans developed into tall beings with extremely flexible cartilaginous skeletons. Strong leg muscles allowed for powerful and quick frog-kick style swimming through water as well as a remarkable jumping ability while on land. Fin-like ears (called [[Haillu/Legends|haillu]]) also aided them in swimming, as well as expressing emotions like aggression, friendship, and fear. They had partially retractable [[Ommatophora|eyestalks]] with nictitating membranes when underwater. They also possessed a unique mucus creating organ that helped when being underwater which they use to stop water from entering their nasal passages and mouth. Green eyes were unusual amongst Gungans.<ref name="GCG">''[[Galactic Campaign Guide]]''</ref>

[[File:JarJarTongue-BlastOff.png|thumb|right|200px|Jar Jar Binks' long tongue]]
Expressive faces and long bills with flaring nostrils were signatures of Gungan physiology. Lengthy muscular tongues and large blunt teeth allowed them to eat lesser amphibians, while a layer of tough skin on the head allowed for burrowing. They had 4 stomachs, to better digest shells and vegetation. A Gungan's arms ended in four digits, and their feet had three stubby toes, both unlike that of a human. Females were smaller with sleeker faces and tended to tie their ears back. Females Gungans with light-colored ear flaps were considered very attractive by male Gungans, while the ones with dark-colored haillu were thought of as 'boyish'.<ref name="GCG" /> As male Gungans aged, some, like [[Roos Tarpals/Legends|Roos Tarpals]], developed prominent whiskers. Both sexes had a lifespan of roughly 65 galactic standard years.<ref name="UAA">''[[Ultimate Alien Anthology]]''</ref>

Gungans had nostrils that sealed when they entered the [[Water/Legends|water]]. They also boasted very strong compound lungs, allowing them to both hold their breath for extended periods of time, breathe underwater, and withstand the pressure of deep water, along with well-padded kneecaps and powerful calves and legs for increased swimming speed. However, because they were so well-adapted to their watery environment, their skin dried easily in hot and arid climates, which [[Jar Jar Binks/Legends|Jar Jar Binks]] experienced during his visit to [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]].

The Gungans appeared to be related to the [[Glurrg]]s, whom they used as a worker caste in their society.

Gungans were detailed in the [[Republic Xenosociological Database]], under Subdirectory ORT831-23,794,928/1N.<ref name="SoN">''[[Secrets of Naboo]]''</ref>

==Society and culture==
{{Quote|My warning you, Gungans no liken outsiders, so don't spect a warm welcome.|Jar Jar Binks|<ref name="Episode I" />}}
[[File:Gungan_High_Council.png|thumb|left|250px|The High Council was the leading body of the Gungan society.]]
Long ago, explorers on Naboo discovered the [[Gung Slabs]], a set of ancient stones engraved with [[Olys Corellisi/Legends|Olys Corellisi]] on one side and [[Old Gungan/Legends|Old Gungan]] on the reverse. These relics, coupled with the work of philologist [[Burro Flats]] of the [[Baobab Archives]], helped [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]] to better understand the culture and language of the Gungan people.

Gungans spoke a variation of Basic known as [[Gungan (language)|Gungan Basic]], or "Gunganese," which occasionally incorporated elements of [[Old Gungan/Legends|Old Gungan]], a language spoken during the time of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Old Republic]]. In fact, the [[Gung Slabs]], a series of ancient monoliths, were essential for the translation of Old Gungan. The Slabs, coupled with the work of philologist [[Burro Flats]] of the [[Baobab Archives]], helped the galaxy to better understand the culture and language of the Gungan people.<ref name="phrasebook">[[Galactic Phrase Book & Travel Guide (real-life book)|''Galactic Phrase Book & Travel Guide'']]</ref> Few Gungans were able to speak the pure Gungan language.<ref name="TPMV">''[[Star Wars: Episode I: The Visual Dictionary]]'' {{C|"Jar Jar Binks"}}</ref>

The later Gungan language was largely a pidgin dialect that most users fluent in [[Galactic Basic Standard/Legends|Basic]] could understand. [[Gungan (language)|Gunganese]], as it was commonly referred to, combined slightly-altered Basic words with the occasional Old Gungan term (i.e. "Seeks doopeewees isa berry good" is translated as "Six landspeeders are very good.")

Utilizing their own unique phraseology, Gungans established a rather successful history of scholarly excellence, albeit unknown to the galaxy at large. Among their achievements include the epic poem ''[[Das Depu Epu Sea]]'', or ''Deep Dark Water''. This ode to [[Da Beauty Al' Round]] was a source of great pride to these noble beings.

[[File:Gungan_society.png|thumb|right|250px|[[Otoh Gunga/Legends|Otoh Gunga]] was the largest Gungan city, home to millions of Gungans and a symbol of their society's unity and strength.]]
Gungan alpha-males often exhibited a series of oral clicks when aggravated or angered. The Gungan [[Gungan Grand Army/Legends|military]] was made up of mostly male volunteers.

Gungans were generally a generous and peaceful race until the Trade Federation invaded. They truly loved to have visitors and warmly welcomed them; however, they would remain suspicious until the visitors had earned their respect.

Gungans were not tolerant of anyone who threatened their peaceful culture. They had very strict laws, and would go to the extremes to punish anyone who had committed a minor crime. Vandals, for example, could be given a sentence of exile, caning, or even stoning.

If a Gungan was cast out of society, it was very difficult for them to return. If they did manage to return legally, they would often be subjected to heavy discrimination. This could make life very difficult for them and could go on for months or years, until their past offenses disappeared from memory. In addition, returning back illegally to the settlement from which they were exiled would sometimes result in the death penalty, especially if they brought along outsiders. It usually required a significant deed to not only have their exile revoked, but also to be welcomed back to the fold, such as the time when Jar Jar Binks, due to his actions in uniting the Gungans and Naboo together to fight the Trade Federation, had his exile revoked and promoted to Bombad General by Boss Rugor Nass.

Gungans were also known to produce [[Force-sensitive/Legends|Force-sensitive]] children and the Gungans [[Kin-Ya Dosun]] and [[Kosa-Yin Hadu]] served as members of the [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]],<ref name="TKAAG">{{LivingForce|Almas, Sweet Almas: The Kaluthin Are Always Greener}}</ref> while the Gungan child [[Roo-Roo Page/Legends|Roo-Roo Page]] was considered as a candidate to receive [[Jedi training/Legends|Jedi training]].<ref name="Children of the Force">{{TCW|Children of the Force}}</ref> The Gungans relied on the semi-sentient mollusk [[Kresch]] for much of their knowledge on matters as varied as Gungan civilization and the fauna of [[Ohma-D'un/Legends|Ohma-D'un]]. The Kresch was consulted by Gungans as an encyclopedia of sorts.<ref name="frontier">[[Star Wars Episode I: The Gungan Frontier|''Star Wars'' Episode I: ''The Gungan Frontier'']]</ref>

Gungans also organized yearly the [[Festival of Warriors]], in which [[Militiagung/Legends|Militiagungs]] gathered to celebrate the Gungan's militaristic culture. An arena was scheduled for construction in [[Lake Umberbool]] for the festivity.<ref name="E1A10">''[[Episode I Adventures 10: Festival of Warriors]]''</ref>

==Religion==
{{Quote|Your gods demand that his life belongs to me now.|[[Qui-Gon Jinn/Legends|Qui-Gon Jinn]]|<ref name="Episode I" />}}
[[File:Gungan_Priest.jpg|thumb|left|150px|A Gungan priest.]]
Gungans were known to venerate certain [[Deity/Legends|deities]] exclusive to their culture known as [[Gud/Legends|guds]],<ref name="CSWE-sacredplace">{{CSWECite|I||Gungan sacred place}}</ref> such as [[Mekamok]], [[Wamka Pol]], [[Balmtop]], [[Dobbis]], [[Kobble]], [[Nododo]], [[Balam]], [[Gob Gobba|Gobba]], and their chief god, [[Oma-Oma]].<ref name="SWGB">''[[Star Wars: Galactic Battlegrounds]]''</ref><ref name="français">Many of these deities were mentioned in the [[Wikipedia:French language|French]] edition of the [[2001]] video game ''[[Star Wars: Galactic Battlegrounds]]'', in the database entry pertaining to the Gungan society, but not in the [[Wikipedia:English language|English]] version of the entry.</ref> By [[1 ABY/Legends|1 ABY]], the fundamentalist sect of the [[Ultragungans]] was active on Naboo. This cult was responsible for stealing an artifact from [[Boss/Legends|Boss]] [[Rugor Nass/Legends|Rugor Nass]], later retrieved by a [[Spacer/Legends|spacer]] hired by the Boss.<ref name="SWG">{{GalaxiesAED}}</ref>

==Military==
''Main Article: [[Gungan Grand Army/Legends|Gungan Grand Army]]''
[[File:Gungans.png|thumb|right|250px]]
The Gungans possessed a large military force, known as the Gungan Grand Army. Most of their transportation were beasts, although there were some biomechanical constructs in one of their heavy weapons. Their vehicles are generally named after native fauna within the Naboo wetlands.

==History==
At some point in Galactic history, there was at least one Otolla Gungan who was a [[Sith/Legends|Sith]].<ref name="SWGS6">{{Topps|set=2011 Topps Star Wars Galaxy Series 6|cardname=#609: The Fallen Gungan|link=https://www.tcdb.com/ViewCard.cfm/sid/75148/cid/5316193/2011-Topps-Star-Wars-Galaxy-Series-6-609-The-Fallen-Gungan}}</ref>

The Gungans were believed to be indigenous to Naboo, but this is uncertain. Biologists believe the Gungans, wherever their original home, evolved originally as land-dwellers.

On Naboo, evidence of Gungan habitation extended for ages, as there are records of battles of survival with the [[woolly veermok]]s during an ice age. However, the primary reason they developed warfare technology was the threat of the [[Bursa/Legends|bursas]] that often attacked their settlements. The Gungans assembled a "Grand Army" to meet this threat, eventually driving the bursas into extinction. Their technology was peculiar in that everything, from tools to structures is not constructed, but "grown", each device being therefore organically unique.

Ancient starfarers told tales of great Gungan migrations across the plains of Naboo prior to their shift to more aquatic environments. The reason most commonly accepted for their flight to the water revolves around an alien civilization of reptilian humanoids remembered as the "[[Elders (Naboo)/Legends|Elders]]," who colonized Naboo. They engaged in warfare with the Gungans, forcing them to retreat underwater, giving rise to modern Gungan civilization. Undoubtedly, the presence of healthful underwater plants and tasty [[gumfish]] did much to solidify their change in lifestyle.

[[File:StimArmor-SWGTCGAoD.jpg|thumb|left|220px|An [[Otolla/Legends|Otolla]] Gungan being assaulted by an Imperial trooper.]]
The Ankura and Otolla branches of Gungans united, forming a symbiotic relationship. They dominated Naboo for millennia afterwards, though largely keeping to the swamps and waterways; the mountains and grasslands were considered 'desert-like'.

About [[3000 BBY]],<ref name="TEA" /> Gungans were separated in tribes that fought against each other ([[War of the Gungan tribes]]), until united under [[Boss/Legends|Boss]] [[Gallo/Legends|Gallo]]. Gungans from various cities migrated to a new large city, [[Otoh Gunga/Legends|Otoh Gunga]], which was the major and capital city of Naboo (as far as Gungans were concerned).

Around five hundred years before the [[Battle of Naboo/Legends|Battle of Naboo]], a number of needy Gungan locals were approached by recruiters sent by [[Hugo Bartyn]]. Bartyn wanted amphibian fishermen to settle a new city in [[Lamaredd/Legends|Lamaredd]] and tempted these poverty-stricken individuals with promises of untouched seas in a new frontier. Once they arrived, however, they became [[Slavery/Legends|slave]] laborers.<ref name="BL">{{GamerCite|7|Bartyn's Landing (article)}}</ref>

The Gungans and the [[Naboo (people)/Legends|Human inhabitants of Naboo]] did not get along, as the Gungans believed the Naboo to be pompous cowards while the Naboo believed the Gungans to be barbarians. This attitude lasted until [[Queen/Legends|Queen]] [[Padmé Amidala/Legends|Amidala]] united the Gungans and Naboo to fight the [[Trade Federation/Legends|Trade Federation]] in the [[Invasion of Naboo/Legends|Battle of Naboo]]. Gungans, over the millennia of [[Human/Legends|Human]] presence, have developed their own dialect based on their [[Galactic Basic Standard/Legends|language]], called [[Gungan (language)|Gungan Basic]].

After the Battle of Naboo, the Gungans attained representation in the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] [[Galactic Senate/Legends|Senate]] through Representative [[Jar Jar Binks/Legends|Jar Jar Binks]]. The Gungans also colonized the moon of [[Ohma-D'un/Legends|Ohma-D'un]], due to overcrowding on Naboo. A number of [[Rorgungans|extremist Gungans]] colonized Naboo's other moon, [[Rori/Legends|Rori]], at about the same time. During the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]] in [[22 BBY/Legends|22 BBY]], a [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|CIS]] biological weapon known as the "[[Swamp gas]]" was unleashed on Ohma-D'un and wiped out much of the population. Later, a Jedi task force defeated the CIS forces on the moon during the [[Battle of Ohma-D'un]], thus saving Naboo.

Following the end of the war, the newly formed [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] established a presence on Naboo. Fearing enslavement, the Gungans went into semi-seclusion. However, Gungan resistance fighters fought a number of [[Imperial vs. Gungan Battle|clashes]] with Imperial forces. At least one Gungan worked on the nearby [[Rori Space Station]].<ref name="SWG" /> After the Empire's defeat at the [[Battle of Endor/Legends|Battle of Endor]] in [[4 ABY/Legends|4 ABY]], the Gungans and the Humans of Naboo banded together once more to oust the Imperial presence from their world, reclaiming the world as free for both species. As a result, the species began traveling in much larger numbers, across Naboo and the galaxy.<ref name=":TWOSW:AFG">''[[The Wildlife of Star Wars: A Field Guide]]''</ref>

===Gungans in the galaxy===
[[File:Gungan_Sith_Galaxy_SWGS6.jpg|thumb|right|160px|An unidentified Otolla Gungan Sith]]
Gungans in Lamaredd achieved certain renown as the co-engineers, along with the [[Quarren/Legends|Quarren]], of the popular [[gondola skimmersub]]. Other Gungans that succeeded in that planet were [[Bamfurd]], a tapcafe owner in [[Bartyn's Landing]];<ref name="BL" /> [[Boom Boom]], the [[Security Chief's Second]]; and [[The Mighty Musstoro]], an Akura wrestler.<ref name="R">{{GamerCite|7|Reckonings}}</ref>

They also jointly operated the [[Dorumaa Resort]] on [[Dorumaa]]'s moon.<ref name="LFCG">''[[Living Force Campaign Guide]]''</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
{{Quote|Where there are no swamps there are no Gungans|A [[bitizen]] through the [[HoloNet/Legends|HoloNet]]|<ref name="TDS">''[[Star Wars: Tiny Death Star]]''</ref>}}
According to an interview with [[George Lucas]], the name "Gungan" came from his son Jett's name for tractors and trucks.<ref name="RollingStone">{{WebCite|url=https://www.rollingstone.com/movies/movie-news/jar-jar-binks-a-digital-star-is-born-50301|text=Jar Jar Binks: A Digital Star Is Born|author=Dunn, Jancee|date=1999-06-24|work=Rolling Stone|archivedate=20200509122715}}</ref>

Gungans were partially modeled after hadrosaurs, duck-billed dinosaurs from the Cretaceous period.

The word "Gungan" can also refer to any member of an Australian genus of frogs, [[Wikipedia:Uperoleia|''Uperoleia'']].<ref>{{WebCite|url=http://www.turtlecare.com.au/difference-between-cane-toads-and-native-australian-frogs.php|text=How to tell the difference between cane toads and native Australian frogs|work=turtlecare|archivedate=20111004080456}}</ref>
